cards.title: Introduction to NuGet Packaging
cards.content:
Packaging in the .NET ecosystem revolves around NuGet. NuGet packages (.nupkg) allow you to share reusable code, libraries, and tools across different projects and teams.

In ASP.NET Core, almost everything—from Entity Framework Core to JSON serializers—is delivered as a NuGet package.

cards.title: Configuring Package Properties
cards.content:
You can configure your project to generate a NuGet package automatically upon build by adding properties directly inside your .csproj file.

<PropertyGroup>
  <PackageId>MyCustom.AspNetCore.Library</PackageId>
  <Version>1.0.0</Version>
  <Authors>Your Name</Authors>
  <GeneratePackageOnBuild>true></GeneratePackageOnBuild>
</PropertyGroup>

pairs.right: Builds the project and creates a .nupkg file
Installs a NuGet package into your project
Uninstalls a NuGet package from your project
Uploads a package to a server like NuGet.org

cards.title: Understanding .nuspec Files
cards.content: A .nuspec file is an XML manifest that describes a package's contents and metadata. While modern SDK-style projects generate this automatically from the .csproj, .nuspec files are still useful for advanced packaging scenarios and complex dependencies.

content.text: To reference a package in an MSBuild project file, you use the <...> XML element with an Include attribute.

steps: Define package metadata (Id, Version, Authors) in the .csproj
Run 'dotnet pack' to compile code and generate the .nupkg file
Test the generated package locally by adding it to a test project feed
Run 'dotnet nuget push' with an API key to publish to the NuGet registry

cards.title: Hosting Private NuGet Feeds
cards.content:
Enterprise applications often require private NuGet feeds to share internal libraries securely. Popular solutions for hosting private feeds include:

  • Azure Artifacts (integrated with Azure DevOps)
  • GitHub Packages
  • BaGet or ProGet (self-hosted options)

You configure access to these feeds using a NuGet.config file in your solution directory.

cards.title: Summary of ASP.NET Core Packaging
cards.content:
You have learned how to:

  • Configure NuGet package properties inside .csproj files.
  • Use .NET CLI commands like pack and push.
  • Manage dependencies with PackageReference.
  • Distribute internal libraries using private feeds.
